A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DESIGNER and the same underlying synthesis pipeline and datasets. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, Qwen3 fine-tuning results, scaling experiments, component ablations, and source-corpus comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Llama fine-tuning experiments, additional dataset comparisons, and expanded data analyses.

M1.justification: The extraction, graph-based deduplication, top-5 retrieval, LLM selection, question synthesis, filtering, and response-generation procedures remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the operational prompts are retained. New design-logic examples illustrate the existing method; additional student models change experimental settings.

E1.justification: v2 removes dedicated solver evaluation on AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and MATH-500, substantially narrowing competition-mathematics coverage while retaining the five multidisciplinary benchmarks. GSM8K is newly included only in difficulty profiling. The underlying 75-discipline DLR corpora and their per-discipline counts remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 adds OpenThoughts3 and Nemotron-Post-Training-v1 to the SFT and dataset-quality comparisons alongside WebInstruct (Full) and NaturalReasoning. Table 3 also adds official Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct comparators. The example-question ablation is renamed rather than newly introduced.

E3.justification: v2 extends SFT evaluation from Qwen3-4B/8B to Llama-3.2-3B and Llama-3.1-8B. The new OpenThoughts3 and Nemotron comparisons retain native CoT responses, unlike the regenerated responses used for the original baselines. Pass@N evaluation is removed. Retained training budgets and generation settings are unchanged; renaming Pass@1 to accuracy is equivalent.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparative disciplinary-distribution analysis and expands difficulty analysis to additional datasets and benchmark questions, while removing the question/response-length analysis and mathematical Pass@N study. Existing component ablations remain, with MMLU-Pro replacing MATH-500 in their reported evaluation. The source-quality control is retained and redisplayed as Figure 6.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 5 adds a shaded variability band around the GPQA-Diamond scaling curve, absent from v1 Figure 2, although its statistical meaning is not explicitly defined. The retained GPQA evaluations still use ten rollouts and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. No new training-seed or repeated-training-run information is supplied.

E6.justification: v2 adds Llama results, OpenThoughts3/Nemotron scores, comparative disciplinary distributions, benchmark difficulty profiles, and MMLU/MMLU-Pro scaling or ablation entries. It removes the length table and AIME/MATH-500 results. Matched Qwen and original baseline-comparison scores are unchanged. WebInstruct's Very Hard proportion changes from 3.59% in v1 Table 3 to 3.57% in v2 Table 10.

T1.justification: The graph-deduplication mathematics, cosine retrieval formula, and five diversity-metric definitions are retained, with the algorithm and metric details moved to Appendices B and G. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs; the new Mermaid examples are illustrative templates.

C1.justification: The design-logic concept and the two 75-discipline dataset contributions remain central. The abstract and introduction broaden the empirical claims from Qwen3-4B/8B to both Qwen3 and Llama3 families and their official instruction-tuned counterparts. v2 also explicitly emphasizes missing question-synthesis guiding principles in prior approaches.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 6.3's explanation of weaker mathematical Pass@1 through the absence of RL and its interpretation of Pass@N as evidence of novel reasoning paths. It also removes the length-based argument for deeper reasoning and adds interpretation of disciplinary imbalance. These changes materially alter the discussion of mechanisms and capability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset URLs and the Nemotron category restriction, identifies the model and corpus used in the existing scaling study, and supplies six Mermaid design-logic examples. Its new reproducibility statement specifies a planned partial data release, without establishing actual availability. Conversely, the shortened decontamination description omits v1's punctuation-handling detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive comparisons with structural-guidance work by Xu et al. (2025), Wang et al. (2025), and Bu et al. (2025), positioning DESIGNER around raw-corpus synthesis and applicability beyond mathematics and coding. KPDDS is reframed from v1's doc-centric example into this external-guidance comparison. Model/dataset references expand, while the RLVR and MATH-500 references disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method descriptions, related work, and conclusion are extensively condensed and rewritten. The standalone Overview disappears, experimental subsections are reordered, and collection, algorithm, metric, and setup material moves into expanded appendices. New reproducibility, ethics, and LLM-use statements further change the document structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds a conceptual illustration, redraws the pipeline, introduces difficulty and discipline-distribution charts, and adds six code/flowchart example figures. The source-quality table becomes a bar chart, the scaling plot changes series and adds shading, and several tables are expanded, reformatted, or relocated. This substantially revises the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens cross-family evidence through Llama experiments, broadens dataset comparisons, and makes design logic more concrete. However, deleting v1 Table 9 removes an important performance boundary: Qwen3-8B trained on DLR-Web+Book scored 53.80 AIME 2025 Pass@1 versus 65.68 for official Qwen3-8B. Removing that section also eliminates its speculative expanded-reasoning interpretation, but leaves the adverse results undisclosed while broad superiority language persists. The gains in evidence and clarity coexist with reduced transparency about limitations, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
